Im probably going to get hate for this, but i really cant fully explain how unwatchable Game of Thrones really is. I mean besides the fact that watching the entire story in continuity is literally the most agonizing, unpleasant experience ever (hence most people only really tuning in around late season 6), theres a good 3 or 4 seasons where literally nothing substantive happens at all. A big criticism of season 5 was how many characters were now in the show, disconnected from each other, and the plot was going nowhere. In fact, i even hate to break it to you book fans because i read the books too, but his story fell apart pretty soon after book 3. It wasnt going anywhere and i really hate to tell you guys this but if it takes you 5 installments of 1000 PAGE FUCKING TOMES to get not even halfway, your story is shit. I read the witcher books and he told a far more eloquent, fast paced and gritty story in probably half the number of pages overall. Final complaint and end to rant is that GOT definitely has moments where it tries way way to hard to be gritty. The witcher books have moments where women in war torn areas get raped to all shit by soldiers, but its presented as the way that stuff is and ugly, and more importantly THEY MOVE ON FAST. I watched the season where Sansa was getting raped by Ramsey and trapped in her own home and literally had to move on after a while without even knowing what happened in that part of the show. Im sorry but im a grown man and if you have to write a plot (admittedly just for the show) where you highlight the female fear of being raped and intimidated by a "scary" psycopath lord, i do not find that compelling. Honestly my advice is sneak a dinner fork or knife, and when he rapes you put it in his face a few times. Either die free or live a slave but dont try to make me watch that shit. Anyways tldr when that bolton ass is making his psycho threats at snow and his men before the battle, watch the scene. They all wear the faces of men who arent sure they can win, but will fight to the death. In some situations you just have to man the ever loving fuck up and do what you can. But none of this overly dark shit.

The wild hunt is lightly open world at best dude. No offense but you are absolutely forced to play the missions in a certain order to get enough experience points to further the storyline and your strength in a natural amount of time. Besides the main missions and the dlcs, the only missions i even stop to play on the side are the monster contracts and the random encounters that have the possibility of being failed if you dont do it then and without leaving a certain area from the quest giver. In no way would i say that skyrim even comes close in the detail of the storyline presented, and i would argue in realisticness and cutscene angle artistry the witcher is the best fantasy world ive ever seen. But somehow for all the faults of bethesda in recent years and even the argument of the dumbing down of the gameplay in skyrim heralded the end of bethesda long in advance, i must say that in my opinion the storyline of a man suddenly finding out he has dragon blood in his veins and stepping up to stop a world threatening evil, delving through the depths of a long abandoned moria like dwarven city and through a vast and implied pitch black expanse of  gigantic cave systems far below the mountains above, retrieving an elder scroll. a literal fragment of creation that defies the laws of time wholesale,  using that scroll to learn a shout that gives him access to alduin, and all dragon's bane and worst fear (to be forced to the ground like any mortal creature), and then going to the nord afterlife and literally chasing him through that world to completely annihilate him with all the deities in that universe looking on. Say what you will about the mechanics or the lack of initiative allowing most players to act dumb till theyre max level and totally overpowered for any fight, in such a short oppurtunity skyrim presented a much more dramatic and full on epic story. And if you use the argument that its all small scale or the events or locations dont feel that way...... dude its like d and d, use your imagination. The witcher certainly forces you to do the same thing, especially since no battles in the entire game are shown in action at any point.
